title: Finding money and handling lost property
summary: Albert says he finds money everywhere and kept a policy for lost items at his club.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Oh, I found lots of money. Dick, I've been lucky all my life. I found $5 bills. I found loads of money. Oh, lots of nickels, dimes, and quads. I look like these things, like magnets. I walk and find them. I have a little pocket with my wallet that I carry with all types of coins and bills that I found. I keep them as a superstition girl. So I'm going to save this, I'll find some more. Which is a common thing for a person to do. And I'll even find a fine man. I found money underneath the sand. I want to be a preacher for a superstition.
What do people leave behind when they're in a nightclub? That's always a thing.

Always quotes, pocket books, earrings, things like that. But I've made a policy that whenever anyone left anything in my club I would say that I had a place for that, especially. And I would keep it in a certain at the time. Then if they didn't call for it, if it missed a grapevine piece I would give it to them and five, ten, and then. Mm-hm.
